translation:
  text: 'After I had finished writing this book, that messenger who had entrusted
    me to this shepherd came into the house where I was and sat down on the couch.
    This shepherd stood at his right hand. Then he called me and said these words
    to me:


    2. “I entrusted you and your household to this shepherd,” he said, “so that you
    might be protected by him.” “Yes, sir,” I said. “If, then, you want protection
    from every affliction and every cruelty,” he said, “and success in every good
    deed and word, and all the strength of righteousness, walk in this one’s commandments,
    which I gave you. Then you will be able to master every evil.”


    3. “For if you keep his commandments, every desire and pleasure of this world
    will be subject to you, and success will follow you in every good undertaking.
    Take his patience and restraint into yourself,[a] and tell everyone that he has
    great honor and dignity before the Lord, that he presides with great authority
    and is powerful in his office. To him alone throughout the whole world has authority
    over repentance been given.[b] Does he seem powerful to you? Yet you all despise
    his patience and the consideration he shows you.”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Maturitas can denote mature gravity, deliberateness or patience. Here the
      shepherd’s restraint and consideration toward offenders favor “patience”; this
      remains a contextual lexical judgment, not a newly attested manuscript reading.
  - marker: b
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: Paenitentia is rendered “repentance” in this moral-change context. The authority
      is assigned to the shepherd in the vision. This clause does not name a later
      church office or identify the shepherd with God.

- source_word: domine

  rationale: Respectful vocative to the visionary interlocutor; divine Dominum remains
    Lord.
- source_word: paenitentia
  chosen: repentance
  alternatives:
  - penance
  - change of mind
  rationale: Context concerns moral return after sins; no later penitential institution
    is inserted.
- source_word: successum in omni opere bono atque verbo
  chosen: success in every good deed and word
  alternatives:

  rationale: Keep the explicit ethical scope; do not turn this into an unrestricted
    wealth promise.
- source_word: maturitatem / modestiam / verecundiam
  chosen: patience / restraint / consideration
  alternatives:
  - gravity / moderation / modesty
  rationale: Distinguish the three expressions in context; footnote exposes maturitas
    ambiguity.
